name: Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Injury
definition: Injury of the MPFL, the main passive restraint to lateral patellar translation, most often occurring with lateral patellar dislocation.

investigations.principle: MRI assesses MPFL and associated osteochondral injury when clinically indicated.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, cartilage, ligament or occult injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Recurrent instability may require MPFL reconstruction with correction of major anatomic risk factors.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-Snayu instability phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Injury of the MPFL, the main passive restraint to lateral patellar translation, most often occurring with lateral patellar dislocation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, unreduced dislocation, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
